AGENDA
  ALHAMBRA YOUTH COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING

  Alhambra Public Library
  Conference Room
  101 S. First Street, Alhambra, CA 91801

  Tuesday, January 8, 2019 - 6:00 p.m.

Commissioners  Members Ex Officio
Amber Gutierrez  Michael Macias,
Anthony Hu  Director of Parks & Recreation
Elisa Jimenez
Selina Martinez  Vincent Hon,
Sophia Olmeda  Recreation Supervisor
Michelle Pham
Madeline Placido
Jaylen Luc
Valerie Gonzalez
Isabella Garcia
Victoria Romero

We welcome you to the Youth Commission meeting.

If you wish to address the Commission during the meeting, please complete a speaker’s card and
give it to the secretary. The maximum time for addressing the Commission is five minutes. If
you wish to address the Commission on an item which appears on the agenda, your comments will
be heard during the Commission’s discussion of that item. If you wish to address the Commission
on a subject which does not appear on the agenda but related to recreation or community service,
you may make your presentation under agenda item VII. Please be advised that the Commission
cannot, under the State of California’s Ralph M. Brown Act, take action on any item which does
not appear on the agenda.

When making your presentation, please give your name and address for the record. Please make
your statement as brief as possible. Thank you.

I.  Roll Call

II.  Flag Salute

III.  Minutes of the Last regular meeting held November 13, 2018
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes of November 13, 2018
  *Note: you must have attended the meeting in order to vote on the minutes.

minutes_text:
APPROVED by: Youth Commission on March 12, 2019

  MINUTES
  Alhambra Youth Commission
  January 8, 2019

The Alhambra Youth Commission was called to order at 6:00 pm on January 8, 2019 at the
Alhambra Public Library Conference Room, 101 S. First Street, Alhambra, CA.

Commission Members Present: Garcia, Jimenez, Martinez, Olmeda and Romero

Commission Members Absent: Duong, Gonzalez, Gutierrez, Hu, Luc, Pham and Placido.

Also present: Vincent Hon, Recreation Supervisor.

III.  APPROVAL OF THE NOVEMBER 13, 2018 YOUTH COMMISSION
  MEETING MINUTES

  On the motion from Commissioner Jimenez and second by Commissioner Garcia
  the Minutes of November 13, 2018 were approved.

IV.  DISCUSSION PERTAINING VOLUNTEER OPPORTUNITIES – TECH
  DAY (SENIOR CENTER)

  Recreation Supervisor Hon asked the Youth Commissioners who were present for
  the December tech day, how the event went. Commissioner Romero stated that many
  of the seniors had various questions some of which she could answer and some of
  which she thought would be better suited to ask their internet provider. She stated
  that they were friendly and eager to learn.

  Recreation Supervisor Hon then provided information to the commissioners
  explaining how their corresponding City Council members will reappoint them to
  become Youth Commissioners again for the new term.

  Recreation Supervisor Hon emphasized that he will try to get the Youth
  Commissioners more tech days and other volunteer opportunities. Mr. Hon has
  recommended including weekends for volunteer opportunities to provide flexibility
  to Youth Commissioners who cannot volunteer during the week. Mr. Hon brought
  up that the approval of more tech days may take until April to be approved as that is
  when the new committee begins the new term. Mr. Hon has suggested a follow up
  procedure for tech day to provide further assistance to the seniors who were
  previously helped the last tech day.

V.  DISCUSSION REGARDING HOLIDAY HOME DECORATING CONTEST
  EXPERIENCE

  Recreation Supervisor Hon asked for feedback from the Youth Commissioners
  about how the Holiday Home Decorating Contest went. Commissioner Garcia
  mentioned that she really enjoyed the opportunity as those participating in the
  contest would come out of their homes and greet the Commissioners.
  Commissioner Garcia mentioned that some homes did not have their lights on
  which made it very hard to judge. Mr. Hon mentioned that houses without their
   lights on should automatically gotten disqualified.
  Commissioner Garcia mentioned that the judging was a bit lengthy and
  transportation could be improved for next year. Recreation Supervisor Hon
  responded that he would try to figure out a way to make transportation for judging
  easier next year. Commissioner Martinez also agreed that transportation could be
  improved and mentioned that a house on the judging list was extremely hard to
  find. All the Commissioners agreed that there were too many houses to judge and
  Commissioner Garcia suggested a tougher process to apply for judging or to
  include a picture for pre-judging. All the commissioners also agreed that the rain
  made the process difficult as well. Mr. Hon suggested different days for judging to
  make the process easier. Commissioner Garcia suggested that stopping by the
  office to pick up the judging packet at an earlier date would make things run more
  smoothly.

  Mr. Hon went on to present the winners of both the Holiday Home Decorating
  Contest and the Office Decorating Contest as well. The commissioners discussed
  their favorite displays of the winners from both contests.

VI.  DISCUSSION REGARDING UPCOMING SPECIAL EVENTS

  Mr. Hon. explained that there are no upcoming special events in February. He does
  mention that there are many upcoming events after February and thus March will
  be a busy month to prep for these events. Recreation Supervisor Hon goes on to
  explain that the next major holiday event is the Easter event April 20th. This event
  is the Spring Eggstravaganza. Afterwards the next event will be Memorial Day and
  then the 4th of July. Mr. Hon offered two volunteer opportunities for the 4th of July
  event consisting of a 2:00pm-6:00pm shift, and a 6:00pm-9:00pm shift, or an all-
  day shift. Commissioner Olmeda mentioned that there wasn’t a big turnout of kids
  for the bouncers during the event last year. Mr. Hon then explained that concerts
  in the park and movies in the park will be happening in the summer as well so
  there are opportunities to volunteer for the rest of the year.

VII.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

  No guest speakers were present for the oral communication portion of the meeting.

VIII. COMMISSION ORALS

  Commissioner Romero explained that there is a stop sign by her school on Marengo
  and Glendon that needs to be more visible. Ms. Romero stated many cars do not stop
  on that stop sign. Mr. Hon stated that he will past the information along to our Public
  Work department.

  Commissioner Olmeda suggested that the 4th of July event should have snapchat
  filters. Mr. Hon stated that last year that we did have a snap chat filter for our
  Pumpkin Run event. Mr. Hon stated that he will set up a snap chat filter for the 4th
  of July event.

  No other Commissioners had anything else to speak about.

XI.  ADJOURNMENT

  The meeting was adjourned at 6:50 p.m. by Recreation Supervisor Vincent Hon.
